title: Rule Benedict chapter 43 permission with non-erasing fault ledger
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Rule Benedict chapter 43 supplies a complete actor-state system in which lateness causes demotion or separation, satisfaction repairs the fault, and an abbot's permission can restore participation while leaving satisfaction due. A finite constructor separates current location from outstanding obligation and tests an exception that does not erase its cause.

source.work: Regula Benedicti, chapter 43, On those who come late to the Work of God or to table
source.source_span: Complete chapter: night office, day Hours, table lateness, repeated failure, refusal and satisfaction/permission clauses.
source.source_limit: The accessed page is Leonard J. Doyle's modern English translation/adaptation of the Latin; it is a source-owned content mechanism, not a target-language identification.

operators: PENANCE(actor,public_scope) -> SATISFIED(actor,domain) only after the written fault is present
PERMIT(actor,authority) -> PERMITTED_WITH_DEBT(actor,domain); location changes but DEBT remains
REENTER(actor,location) -> PARTICIPATING(actor,location) only after permission or satisfaction according to the branch
COUNT(actor,domain,n) -> THRESHOLD_STATE(actor,excluded) when the source's repeated-lateness condition is met
REFUSE(actor,offered_item) -> DEBT(actor,refusal_domain) with the same satisfaction requirement
constructor.evaluation_order: LATE or REFUSE opens a debt; PERMIT may change current location; PENANCE/SATISFACTION closes the debt; REENTER records current participation. No operator may delete DEBT merely by changing LOCATION.
constructor.consequence: A single actor can be in the permitted choir while still owing satisfaction. Later satisfaction remains required, and repeated table lateness changes common participation to separation. The model therefore predicts a cross-clause state where LOCATION=choir and DEBT=true coexist.
constructor.rival: R-CLEAR treats permission as erasing the fault: PERMIT(actor,authority) directly yields PARTICIPATING with no debt. It predicts no later satisfaction obligation after permitted re-entry and cannot preserve the chapter's exception wording.
constructor.falsifier: Reject if the complete source branch makes permission erase the duty of satisfaction, if repeated table lateness has no threshold/state change, or if a target-side complete passage cannot carry actor, location and obligation as distinct typed fields. A repeated word is not credited as the same actor without an explicit context/identity rule.
constructor.source_content_consequence: The distinctive test is non-commutation: PERMIT then PENANCE is defined, while PENANCE before LATE is undefined and PERMIT without a preceding debt is not an exception. This is an obligation-persistence consequence, not a generic OPEN/UPDATE/CLOSE label.

Exception/scope relations are a broad predecessor without this actor-location/debt separation.
Administrative scope is a nearby rival; this card requires a persistent obligation across domains.
